text:
### Observed differences

- A09 and A16 exchanged their participation levels. In the earlier window, A09 ran in every trace, about twice per trace, with repeats in roughly 48 in 100 traces; in the later window, it runs in about 97 of 200 traces (about half), about once per trace, and never repeats. A16 moved the opposite way: from about 100 of 200 traces with a single occurrence to all 200 traces, about 1.85 occurrences per trace, with repeats in about 44 in 100 traces. [OCC007, OCC013]
- Their typical placement also exchanged: A09's mean relative position moved from about 0.68 to about 0.45 of the trace, while A16's moved from about 0.39 to about 0.70. [POS008, POS015]
- Direct succession rewired in a mirrored way. A04 and A10, whose outgoing transitions previously went exclusively to A09, now go exclusively to A16; A01 and A13, which previously could lead to A16 (about 20 and 23 in 100 of their outgoing transitions), now lead to A09 instead (about 18 and 27 in 100), with A16 no longer observed among their successors. A09's own outgoing transitions changed from mainly A06 (about 50 in 100), A05 and A14 to A10, A04, A01 and A13, while A16's changed from A10, A04, A01 and A13 to mainly A06 (about 54 in 100), A05 and A14 — the two successor sets effectively exchanged. [DIR004, DIR007, DIR001, DIR009, DIR006, DIR011]
- Step distances mirror the same exchange: A01→A09 moved from 2–4 steps to 1–2 steps while A01→A16 moved from 1–2 to 2–4 steps; A09→A04 moved from mostly 5 steps to 1–3 steps while A16→A04 moved from 1–3 to mostly 5 steps; A09→A06 and A09→A10 similarly traded places with A16→A06 and A16→A10. [LAG004, LAG010, LAG026, LAG065, LAG028, LAG067, LAG031, LAG070]
- Co-occurrence with the rest of the process flipped accordingly: A09 now co-occurs with A01, A03, A06, A13 and A18 in only about 49 in 100 traces (previously all) and no longer with A15 (about 50 in 100 before, none after); A16 now co-occurs with A01, A03, A06, A13 and A18 in every trace, and A15 and A16, previously strict alternatives that never appeared together, now appear together in about 52 in 100 traces. [REL007, REL037, REL076, REL108, REL110, REL014, REL044, REL137, REL143]
- Independently of this exchange, several activities occur or repeat less in the later window: A07 (mean 1.33 → 0.85; present in 72 → 57 of 200 traces), A12 (mean 2.32 → 1.70), A05 (mean 1.24 → 0.89 with participation unchanged at about 39 in 100 traces, i.e., fewer repeats) and A14 (mean 1.08 → 0.82); A12 also routes relatively less to A07 (about 57 → 50 in 100) and more to A08. [OCC005, OCC010, OCC004, OCC011, DIR008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A09 and A16 exchanged their roles in the process flow. In the earlier window, A09 was a mandatory, repeated, late activity (in all 200 traces, about twice each, around two-thirds into the trace, followed mainly by A05, A14 and A06), while A16 was an optional, single, earlier activity (in half the traces, followed by A01, A04, A10 and A13); in the later window these roles are reversed — A16 is mandatory, repeated and later, A09 is optional, single and earlier, A04 and A10 now lead into A16 instead of A09, and A01 and A13 lead into A09 instead of A16. [OCC007, OCC013, POS008, POS015, DIR004, DIR007, DIR001, DIR009, DIR006, DIR011]

The pattern is direct and consistent: participation, recurrence, position, direct-succession and step-distance evidence all change in the same mirrored direction, and each key item exceeds the differences seen in about 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data, so sampling variation alone is an unlikely explanation for the pattern as a whole. [OCC007, OCC013, POS008, POS015, DIR004, DIR007, DIR006, DIR011, LAG004, LAG010]

Limitations: the many relation and lag items largely re-express this single underlying change rather than confirming it independently, and the evidence contains no screening expectation, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with what an unchanged process would produce; the evidence shows that the roles exchanged, but not the mechanism behind it. A competing explanation that cannot be fully excluded is that the two windows sample different mixes of process variants rather than one modified flow, although the all-or-nothing participation exchange makes plain sampling noise unlikely. [REL007, REL110, REL143, LAG026, LAG065]

Other differences: A07, A12, A05 and A14 occur or repeat less often in the later window (A07 in 72 → 57 of 200 traces; A12 mean 2.32 → 1.70; A05 mean 1.24 → 0.89 with unchanged participation; A14 mean 1.08 → 0.82), with A12 routing relatively more to A08 and less to A07; the evidence does not establish whether these shifts are connected to the A09/A16 exchange. [OCC005, OCC010, OCC004, OCC011, DIR008]
